full_judgment:
The respondent No. 3 International finance Investment and Commerce Bank Ltd. (IFIC Bank), as plaintiff, instituted Artha Rin Case No. 12 of 1997 on 12-6-97 in the Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj against the petitioner and respondent No. 4 for recovery of Bank loan amounting to Taka 24,31,457 contending, inter aria, that the defendant No. 1 is an importer and borrower, defendant No. 2 is the guarantor of the loan availed by the defendant No. 1. The suit was decreed on 15-1-2003 against defendant No. 2 on contest and against defendant No. 1 ex parte for an amount of Taka 24, 31, 457 with interest at the rate of 15.50% and the decree was drawn up on 5-1-2004. The decree-holder Bank filed Artha Rin Execution Case No. 78 of 2004 on 22-4-2004 for realization of Taka 67,77,914 The decree-holder on 26-4-2006 filed an application stating that the judgment-debtors are avoiding of service. So, for realization of loan, it is necessary to issue a warrant of arrest. 

 3. Thereafter on 24-9-2006 the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj allowed the petition of decree-holder and issued a warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors. The judgment-debtors challenged the impugned order dated 24-9-2006 and filed the instant writ petition. 

 4. Mr Mrinal Kanti Biswas, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that so long vires of section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 has already been decided by number of judgments delivered by the High Court Division as well as by the Appellate Division, he does not press the rule in respect of the section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Next he submits that it appears that the application under section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for issuing the warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors, the concerned official/authority of the Bank neither put his signature nor made any verification/affidavit thereto and therefore, it cannot be said that the application in question was filed by the decree-holder Bank as per Provision of section 34(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 as such, the rule should be made absolute. 

 6. We have examined the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition and the materials on record. We have examined the application filed on behalf of the decree-holder Bank (Annexure-C to the supplementary affidavit). It appears that the application has been filed by the learned Advocate on behalf of the Bank but the application is neither signed by the official/authority of the Bank nor the application contains the verification/affidavit thereto and therefore, it cannot be said that the application in question was filed by the decree-holder Bank as per Provision of section 34(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. 

 "We have carefully examined the application under section 34 of the AM, 2003, it appears that in the application under section 34 of the Ain, 2003 for issuing warrant of arrest against the judgment debtors the concerned official/authority of the Bank neither put his signature nor made any verification/affidavit thereto and therefore, it cannot be said that the application in question was filed by the decree-holder-Bank as per provision of section 34(1) of the AM, 2003. Accordingly, we find substance and force in the submission of the learned, Advocate for the petitioner on this point."
